sara_support: :rotating_light: ACME reported a p99 jump on /v1/generate around 09:15 UTC. p95 looks fine (~200-300ms) but p99 is up to ~1.5s. No 5xxs, just higher tail latency. sample request ids: r-abc123, r-def456. they say it happens on low-burst traffic (few concurrent users). attaching small log snippet they pasted below. can someone triage?

mike_oncall: looking. grabbing per-node batcher metrics now. were there any recent batcher/runtime config changes?

jess_sre: not that i'm aware of in prod, but we had a config patch last night for continuous-batcher tuning. @mike_oncall can you check deploy history?

ci-deploy-bot: config-deploy: "batcher-linger-tweak" rolled out by deploy-cd at 2959995200 (23:47 UTC). Files changed: continuous_batcher.linger_ms: 25 -> 5, batcher.early_flush.enabled: true

mike_oncall: aha. that aligns. lowering linger_ms to 5 was intended to reduce avg latency for large throughput. but on low-burst patterns it looks like we're seeing lots of tiny batches (size=1/2) -> more kernel invocations and KV cache churn. this increases tail for some requests. i'm pulling batch-size histogram and kernel latency distribution.

mike_oncall: quick repro for others: send 1 req every 120ms for 5m to a gen node, you should see many single-item batches and p99 increase. e.g.
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'; sleep 0.12; done
```
Also query metrics: `curl -s "http://metrics.internal/api/query?m=batcher_batch_size_count&node=<node>"`

raj_runtime: yep. lowering linger made the batcher flush earlier and early_flush=true forces small batches out rather than waiting for coalescing. For high qps that helps, but for sparse arrivals it creates high per-batch overhead. We're seeing a ~3-4x increase in GPU kernel startup jitter and KV cache invalidation on affected nodes.

jess_sre: any quick mitigations we can do while we evaluate?

mike_oncall: 1) revert the linger_ms change back to 25 on the affected pool (quick config rollback) 2) disable `batcher.early_flush` until we have a nuanced policy 3) enable a temporary routing rule to route low-qps customers through a nodepool with lower concurrency but more batching-friendly settings. I can do 1+2 now.

mike_oncall: rolling back now -> deploying config revert (rollback commit: abcdef123).

ci-deploy-bot: config-deploy: "rollback-batcher-linger" rolled out by deploy-cd at 2960000100 (00:15 UTC). Files changed: continuous_batcher.linger_ms: 5 -> 25, batcher.early_flush.enabled: false

mike_oncall: rollback complete. monitoring p99. initial signs: p99 back down to ~260ms on the affected nodes. still watching for a minute to ensure stabilization.

jess_sre: great. please open a follow-up to investigate a smarter policy: adaptive linger based on instantaneous QPS + per-customer routing option. also add a canary guard so changes to batcher params only touch a small % of nodes.

raj_runtime: i'll take the follow-up. action items: (1) add canary rollout in deploy config, (2) instrument per-batch kernel startup and kv-cache-miss metric, (3) simulation test for low-burst workloads.

mike_oncall: filed SRE-4521 with logs and repro. adding runbook note: if p99 spike correlates with low-burst QPS and recent batcher changes, revert linger_ms and disable early_flush.

sara_support: passing back to customer. thanks all. :thumbsup:
